## Step 0 — preflight

1. Resolve `{repo}`, `{REPO}`, `{USER}`, `{session}` (workflow.md).
2. Tools: `tmvp version` — missing is a **hard stop** (give the install command: `curl -fsSL …/install.sh | sh`). `sec --version` — missing → variables come from env-file names only; note it. `gh auth status` only if the remote is GitHub.
3. If `{session}` exists: show the round header, the decisions in 3 lines, then ask the **unanswered questions verbatim** (plus "or start over?"). Stop.
4. New session: one line — "I'll scan read-only, then ask about projects, environments, systems and the questions agents will ask; I write nothing until you approve the plan." Then the standing commands in one line (`defaults · why · skip · back <step> · map · pause`). Go to step 1.

## Step 1 — scan (no questions)

Read `references/evidence.md`. Collect, with file:line evidence:

1. **Units** — every buildable/deployable folder: manifests (go.mod, package.json workspaces, pyproject, pom/gradle modules, Cargo members, Dockerfile*), and what deploys them (Kamal `config/deploy*.yml`, compose, helm/k8s, CI deploy jobs). Note which units share a data store.
2. **Environment names** — CI workflow names/`environment:` keys, Kamal destinations, k8s namespaces/contexts (names), terraform workspaces, `sec project ls`, and env-file names from `tmvp env-keys` (e.g. `.env.production`, `application-dev.env` → `dev`).
3. **Variables** — `tmvp env-keys {repo}` (names only) and, per env, `sec env ls <env>` / `sec ls --json`. Also names read in code (`os.Getenv`, `process.env.`, `os.environ`, `@Value("${…}")`, compose `environment:`). Build: variable → which env files define it (set/empty) → which code reads it → which system it implies (`DATABASE_URL`/`POSTGRES_*` → postgres, `REDIS_*` → redis, `S3_*`/`AWS_*` → aws, `*_API_KEY` of a SaaS → http …).
4. **Systems** — from deploy files, infra folders, drivers/clients in code and the variables above. Type hints: `references/systems/README.md` and `references/systems/<type>.md`.
5. **Data** — for each data store: migrations/models → tables; repositories/DAOs → the real queries (evidence.md "queries people actually run").

Write all of it under `## Findings` in `{session}`. Then go to step 2.

## Step 2 — projects (blast radius)

Show the units table: folder · what it is · deploys as · data stores · marker (✓ ~ ?).
Rule to explain once: one project = one skill = the systems an agent working there can reach. Folders sharing a DB/queue belong together; folders with their own stores can stand alone. Folders may be combined freely or left out (docs, tooling).

Round A: how many projects and which folders (questions.md, step 2 rows 1–2). One unit → just confirm the name.
Round B: who uses the skill and for what; shared libraries; cross-repo deploys (rows 3–5) — skip rows that are ✓.

Stop after each round. Record in `{session}` → `## Decisions`. Then step 3.

## Step 3 — environments (per project; later projects: "same as <first> except…?")

Show env names with evidence and markers; propose merges (`production`/`prod`, `application-dev.env`/`.env.dev`) and drop non-envs (`sample`, `example`, `ci`, `test`).

Round A: names · each env's `type:` (prod / staging / dev / test / local — there may be many envs of one type, e.g. 100 dev or 20 prod) · default env (questions.md step 3 A). Write `type:` on every env; prod-type envs are always protected.
Round B: shared stores between envs · `local` · several targets per env · naming vs sec scope (step 3 B).
A store shared with prod is protected in every env that uses it — say so when it happens.

Stop after each round. Record in `{session}`. Then step 4.

## Step 4 — systems and variables (per project; later projects start "same as <first> except…?")

Rounds in order, one topic each, ≤ 3 questions (rows in questions.md step 4). Skip a round whose findings are all ✓.

- **A matrix** — systems (name · type) × envs: `✓/~/? evidence` or `missing`, and how it is reached if known.
- **B reach & login** — via which host/bastion/VPN, ssh alias and key *path*, read-only DB user or app login. Never dial anything to find out.
- **C variables & gaps** — every variable: envs/files defining it (set/empty) · in sec as `<project>@<env>:NAME`? · config slot. Triage unmapped names into CI-only / app config / unknown; ask only about unknown. Gaps → owner command (`sec import <file> --project <p> --env <e>` or `sec set …`).
- **D sensitivity & budget** — PII/secret-looking tables (from migrations) → excluded or counts-only; prod limits.
- **E SaaS & observability** — which third-party APIs matter; where they look first when prod breaks.

Record systems, reach, variable map, `## Sensitivity` in `{session}`. Then step 4b.

## Step 4b — what will agents ask? (brainstorm, ~5 min, optional)

Goal: the saved-query (and saved-script/api) list, from real needs, not just code.

1. Ask: "Which 3 questions did you last answer by hand on prod?" Stop.
2. Offer 8–10 candidates seeded from code: repository/DAO queries, admin pages, job/status columns, error tables, the lookups code does most (by id, by email). Each: name · one-line description · params · system · envs.
3. One question per turn: pick, add, rename, drop. Stop when the user says "enough" (or `defaults` = top 5).
4. Apply sensitivity: no PII columns — ids and counts; every query cheap (indexed filter or `limit`).

Write the list to `{session}` → `## Saved queries`. Then step 5.

## Step 5 — the plan (approval gate)

Write the plan into `{session}` under `## Plan` and show it in full:

```
Project <name>  →  .agents/skills/<name>-tmvp/   (linked: .claude/skills/<name>-tmvp)
  folders: …          users: on-call, support
  envs: dev (default), staging (shares dev DB), prod (protected)
  systems:
    box   ssh       dev prod   alias …, key ~/.ssh/… (path only)
    db    postgres  dev prod   via box · sec <name>@<env>:DATABASE_URL · app login (RO user = owner step)
    gh    gh        all        repo owner/name
  sensitivity: users.email, tokens → excluded; payments → counts only
  prod budget: limit 50, 10s, indexed filters
  references: projects.md, environments.md, db.md, box.md, gh.md
  saved queries: counts-by-status(days), stuck-jobs(minutes), user-by-id(id) …
  owner steps: sec import …, sec set …
  REPLACE_ME left: …
  defaulted (please glance): …
  left out (and why): …
Then: validate → check → prove each system → run every saved query in every env → sync/lint → report.
```

Ask: "{USER}, approve this plan, or change something?" Stop. Only explicit approval moves to step 6; a change reopens its step (`back <step>`), redoing only what depends on it, and shows the diff.

## Step 6 — build (only after approval)

Track a checklist under `## Progress` in `{session}`; update it as you go.

Per project:
1. `tmvp new skill <project> --from <existing config>` if one exists, else `tmvp new skill <project> --envs <e1,e2,…>` (links `.claude/skills/`).
2. Write `config.yaml` per `references/wiring.md` and `references/systems/<type>.md`; secrets as `$file(sec get <project>@<env>:NAME --out ${out})`; prod envs `destructive: false`; unknowns `REPLACE_ME`.
3. `tmvp --skill <dir> validate`, then `check` (all envs). Fix config errors yourself. A blocker you can't fix (login, missing secret) → note it, keep going.
4. One "prove it" read per system (`references/wiring.md`). For data stores run `ls` and `describe` on the main tables.
5. Write `references/` and `assets/` per `references/output.md`: projects.md, environments.md, one `<system>.md` each (data stores: databases, tables from code confirmed live, table → code users), saved read-only queries from the code. Every command in them is a tmvp command.
6. Run every saved query in every env (`tmvp --skill <dir> all <db> @<name> …`); fix or drop the ones that fail.
7. `tmvp --skill <dir> skill sync` (SKILL.md lists the references) and `skill lint`.

Report to {USER}: per project, env × system → ok / blocker; saved queries written; owner steps (exact commands); what was left out. Ask whether to commit — never commit unasked.
